source.publicationBasis: Assigned detailed-pass researcher confirmed this record contains public source context; browser read

text:
Browser observations on 2026-10-06. Public Phabricator pages were read through the browser. Timeline includes visible inline change requests, not merely revision summary. Exact quoted text follows each URL. This record contains focused evidence excerpts and interpretations, not a complete archive. No remote review state changed.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212079
Accepted May29, reopened after upstream backout June3, then abandoned. No substantive inline request visible. Acceptance alone does not establish the parser behavior persisted.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D211935
Reviewer: "OK, does LGTM, but I'm a little bit worried re automation, is this going to bite us on the backside any time upstream bits change?"
Author: "Potentially it could. The upstream crate code doesn't churn nearly as much though, I think we can proceed for now without it."
Accepted gtest linkage; manual upstream crate copy risk remains.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D210061
https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D210062
Accepted CI/configuration change. No substantive inline change requests visible. Related Rust gtest dependency matters to enabling normal builds.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D210934
Reviewer: "My preference would be to not use a loop for this, and to instead explicitly assert sort order, await the view rebuild, and then explicitly assert again."
Reviewer explains the pattern as "check, modify, check again".
Reviewer: "Does it make sense to call SaveSortInfo() inside UpdateSortInfo(), since they're logically related and SaveSortInfo() is called everywhere UpdateSortInfo() is?"
Author: "I thought about that too, but I think keeping it separate makes it clearer where SaveSortInfo() is called everywhere (and a little easier to search for)."
Review also simplified helper contract wording and asked braces on touched single-line if conditions. Final patch kept explicit save call and explained when helper must be called and what it does not update.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D211998
Inline request: "nitpick: might be better to use @Test, or @example.org for test messages"
Marked done; final sample08.eml uses john@example.com. Treat this as test-fixture convention evidence, not a literal requirement for only example.org.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212152
Author inline twice: "C string literals are not supported in our MSRV."
Reviewer: "This looks good and also fixed my local build"
MSRV means minimum supported Rust version. No local build reproduced by this study.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D210487
Reviewer: "Seems updateMessageCount would be a better name"
Reviewer: "It's generally not a great idea to have a variable with the same name as a function, unless the variable is a function (yay, JS!). I would either call it shouldUpdateMessageCount or flip the meaning and call it skipUpdateMessageCount."
Reviewer: "It only needs to be called when we're changing folder, not every time we change the view, which is how we get into trouble with quick filtering."
Final design removed this boolean rather than landing either suggested boolean name. Timeout/multiple-trigger workaround replaced by lifecycle change. Reviewer accepted with a remaining filtered synthetic deletion edge discussed.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D209591
Accepted NSS export addition. No substantive inline change request visible.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D210737
Reviewer: "nitpick: NS_ENSURE_ARG_POINTER() isn't quite right here, since it's not an argument. NS_ENSURE_STATE() might be more appropriate."
Author: "The nsPop3Sink passes messages though the parser one at a time. After each message, nsPop3Sink::IncorporateComplete() publishes it. The parser should never ever see mbox "From " separators."
Reviewer requested a regression test before landing. Body From-line fixture and message/database header assertions landed. Body-equality defect found by this study is an independent source observation.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212502
Bulk old profile migration removal accepted. Read context only; excluded deleted implementation from detailed study.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212537
https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212839
Initial l10n-bump shape update accepted; later default-branch URL followup accepted. No substantive inline discussion visible.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212552
Author: "For review purposes, the code-review job has two additional jobs I manually added: L10n-pre and L10n-pre-S"
Required artifacts named "strings_all.tar.zst" and "l10n-changesets.json (only on -S variant)". Compare archive contents and JSON output shape against release artifacts. Accepted.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212116
https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D213242
Initial ESR release-note change and later release-types selector correction accepted. No substantive inline requests visible.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D211914
Summary: "We should only use id inside a primary type definition."
Example explains MailFolder owns id; a MailFolder used elsewhere should use named folderId. MailTab uses tabs API IDs; ComposeRecipient contacts/mailinglist node IDs; spaces query uses spaceId. MV3 gate deliberately preserves MV2. Accepted by mkmelin; Standard8 supported idea and asked full Thunderbird reviewer.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212576
Reviewer reported previously failing test passes. Accepted exact expected-object update adding world:ISOLATED.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212030
Related inline images should use existing listAttachments/getAttachmentFile APIs and expose contentId; accepted. A suggestion to remove content-disposition gating must be checked against landed code, which still contained it at this revision.

SUPPLEMENTAL CURRENT ACCEPTED CORRECTIONS (outside assigned chronology coverage):
https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D262633
Author final update: "Update the folder pane colors test to cope with the new colors and test in both light and dark mode. Also fix resetting with the new color values."
Initial2025 color patch backed out for tests; updated tests/semantic reset state relanded. Current folderColors can use light-dark.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D238186
Summary: "The only set of parts which should be excluded are inline text parts, which are reported by the dedicated messages.listInlineTextParts() method."
Binary inline MIME parts classified as attachments. Reviewer requested nullable string return documentation, accepted after update.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D273796
Summary: "This part is specified as inline and has no name. The former implementation treated it as an attachment, excluded it's body from getFull(), which was wrong."
Author notes two existing tests locked wrong behavior; all parts still reported as attachments or inline text parts. Accepted Nov25,2025.

https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D273921
Discussion: one worker's synchronous native calls block its event loop, serializing DNS requests; PromiseWorker itself resolves matching promises and is not the reason native calls are serialized.
Author: "That was a good tip. I added a registration to shut down the thread prior to web worker shutdown."
Reviewer: "this is to avoid potential threading issues as the non res_n* functions are using global shared state."
Accepted Dec1,2025. Followup2003284 for native lookup implementation; no claim it was completed here.
title: Browser review and inline evidence for history228–257 and current corrections
